10.name: TomlInteger
10.docs:
Helper struct for formatting TOML integers.

This may be constructed by calling [`TomlIntegerFormat::format()`].

8.name: format
8.docs:
Formats `value` as a TOML integer.

Returns `None` if the value cannot be formatted
(e.g. value is negative and the radix is not decimal).

359.name: value
359.docs:
Write an encoded TOML scalar value To customize the encoding, see - [`TomlStringBuilder`][crate::TomlStringBuilder] - [`TomlIntegerFormat`][crate::TomlIntegerFormat]
For floats, this preserves the sign bit for [`f32::NAN`] / [`f64::NAN`] for the sake of format-preserving editing. However, in most cases the sign bit is indeterminate and outputting signed NANs can be a cause of non-repeatable behavior. For general serialization, you should discard the sign bit. For example: ``` # let mut v = f64::NAN; if v.is_nan() { v = v.copysign(1.0); } ```

5.name: as_hex_lower
5.docs: Sets the format to hexadecimal with all characters in lowercase.

4.name: as_hex_upper
4.docs: Sets the format to hexadecimal with all characters in uppercase.

356.name: key
356.docs:
Write an encoded TOML key

To customize the encoding, see [`TomlStringBuilder`][crate::TomlStringBuilder].
